idiom_name: for/while loop carrying the accumulator, optionally driven by a function pointer with a void* context
implementation_notes: C has no generics, no closures and no fold in the standard library, so the pattern is written by hand: the traversal is a loop (over an array with an index or pointer walk, over a list via the next pointers) and the combine step is either inlined or passed as a function pointer with a void* context - the calling convention the C standard library itself uses for callbacks, where qsort_s hands its comparison function a void* context for exactly this reason. Generic folds in C are therefore typed loosely (void* accumulator, element size in bytes, a combine function that mutates the accumulator) and are worth it only in library code that must accept arbitrary element types; inside one program the written-out loop is clearer, faster and type-safe because the compiler sees every step.
pitfalls: The accumulator is untyped and mutated through a void*: ownership, size and aliasing are the caller's problem, and a combine that produces a different type needs a second out-parameter instead of a return value.

A recursive fold over a deep list or tree has no tail-call guarantee: -O2 sibling-call optimization often removes a self-recursive call, but -O0, other compilers and any fold that combines both children before returning keep one frame per level, so input-driven depth needs an explicit loop or stack.

Nothing checks the identity: an uninitialized or wrong initial accumulator (0 for a product, NULL for a string builder) shows up only as a wrong result, and never on empty input where it matters most.

variants.name: Recursive case fold over a tagged node type (hand-written catamorphism)
variants.idiom_name: one recursive function per algebra, switching on the node tag
variants.implementation_notes: The structural form of the pattern: a node type with a tag and a union, and one recursive function that switches on the tag and combines the already-folded children - the catamorphism written out by hand, which is what a C program does for expression trees, JSON-like documents and other recursive data. Because C has no exhaustiveness check, the switch needs a reachable default that aborts (plus -Wswitch-enum -Werror as a build-time guard), otherwise a new tag falls through to the end of the function and produces whatever the missing return leaves behind. Parameterising the recursion over the algebra requires a function pointer per case and a context struct; extract that only when a second or third fold over the same shape actually appears.
pitfalls: Without a default that aborts, a switch over tags has no exhaustiveness guarantee at all: an unhandled tag runs off the end of the function instead of failing at the case, and -Wswitch only helps while a default is absent and the tag is an enum.

Stack depth equals data depth: a fold that combines two children before returning cannot be a sibling call, so deeply nested documents overflow the stack long before memory is exhausted - an explicit worklist is the fix.

Writing a second algebra means duplicating the recursion unless the case functions are extracted behind function pointers with a context struct, and that indirection makes the hot path measurably slower than the direct recursion.
